##### Summary

The v-number of a graded ideal is an invariant recently introduced in the context of coding theory, particularly in the study of Reed–Muller-type codes. In this work, we study the localized v-numbers of a binomial edge ideal associated to a finite simple graph G. We introduce a new approach to compute these invariants, based on the analysis of transversals in families of subsets arising from dependencies in certain rank-two matroids. This reduces the computation of localized v-numbers to the determination of the radical of an explicit ideal and provides upper bounds for these invariants. Using this method, we explicitly compute the localized v-numbers of at the associated minimal primes corresponding to minimal cuts of G. Additionally, we determine the v-number of binomial edge ideals for cycle graphs and give an almost complete answer to a conjecture from Dey et al.

Asymptotic behavior of integer programming and the v-function of a graded filtration

Article

Full-text available

  * May 2025
  * J ALGEBRA APPL

  * Antonino Ficarra
  * Emanuele Sgroi

The v-function of a graded filtration ℐ = {I[k]}k≥0 is introduced. Under the assumption that ℐ is Noetherian, we prove that the v-function v(I[k]) is an eventually quasi-linear function. This result applies to several situations, including ordinary powers, and integral closures of ordinary powers, among others. As another application, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of certain integer programming problems. Finally, we present the Macaulay2 package VNumber.

#### Improved Upper Bounds for the Rank of the Determinant Tensor via Glynn's Formula

Jeong-Hoon Ju, Hayoung Choi and Taehyeong Kim

In this paper, we improve the upper bound for the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ determinant tensor to $\mathcal{B}_n-2^{n-1}+n+1$ by finding a new tensor decomposition of the tensor, where $\mathcal{B}_n$ denotes the $n$-th Bell number. The main idea is to replace a part of the tensor decomposition suggested by Houston–Goucher–Johnston with a tensor that is essentially the same as the $n \times n$ permanent tensor, and to use Glynn's formula. This upper bound gives an improved upper bound for the Waring rank of the $n \times n$ determinant polynomial for $n \geq 17$ as well.

#### Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms

Meghana Bhat, Enrico Carlini, Shreedevi K. Masuti et al. (+1 more)

The complete intersection forms are the homogeneous polynomials whose annihilator ideal or the Macaulay dual, is an Artinian complete intersection ideal. In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal. Further, we also compute the Waring rank of the product of binary forms in different sets of variables.

#### Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals

Emiliano Liwski

We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.
